1. Nat Neurosci. 2000 Nov;3(11):1077-8. doi: 10.1038/80586.

Impaired recognition and experience of disgust following brain injury.

Calder AJ(1), Keane J, Manes F, Antoun N, Young AW.

Author information:
(1)MRC Cognition and Brain Sciences Unit, 15 Chaucer Road, Cambridge CB2 2EF, 
UK. andy.calder@mrc-cbu.cam.ac.uk

Huntington's disease can particularly affect people's recognition of disgust 
from facial expressions, and functional neuroimaging research has demonstrated 
that facial expressions of disgust consistently engage different brain areas 
(insula and putamen) than other facial expressions. However, it is not known 
whether these particular brain areas process only facial signals of disgust or 
disgust signals from multiple modalities. Here we describe evidence, from a 
patient with insula and putamen damage, for a neural system for recognizing 
social signals of disgust from multiple modalities.

DOI: 10.1038/80586
PMID: 11036262 [Indexed for MEDLINE]
